key_insight: CloakFEM shows that valid, solvable FEM programs can act as efficiency attacks, increasing solver iterations by up to 5,752.72×.
engineering_relevance: Simulation services may face computational denial-of-service risks even when submitted FEM models run successfully.
method: Use an LLM agent to search for FEM programs that amplify solver computation.
Represent candidates with an FEM-specific intermediate representation.
Apply a deterministic validity gate to enforce runnable constraints.
evidence_signal: Across three FEM stacks, 17 problem classes, and 1,068 seeds, CloakFEM outperformed five generic black-box baselines; the extreme case increased iterations from 43 to 247,367.
watch_item: The reported peak amplification concerns iteration count, not necessarily equivalent wall-clock slowdown, and vulnerabilities vary by problem and solver.
paper_title: CloakFEM: Agentic FEM Code Generation for Red-Teaming Computational Resource Exhaustion
